about.title: A catalogue that separates names, evidence and importance.
about.intro: Cognitive biases do not form a perfectly bounded scientific list. This site preserves disagreements, overlaps and limitations instead of hiding them.
about.level_text: Each card gives a name, a concise explanation, an example and a provisional importance score. The full entry adds mechanisms, nuances, safeguards and sources.
about.evidence_text: Practical importance reflects a bias's potential reach. Scientific strength reflects the quality and convergence of the available research. The two dimensions remain separate.
about.evolving_text: This version publishes {count} cards: {reviewed} reviewed, {reviewing} under review and {not_reviewed} not reviewed. Every status and review date comes from the card's Markdown file.
about.quote: “Let us then strive to think well: that is the principle of morality.”
about.quote_source: Blaise Pascal, Pensées, Transition fragment 6 — Lafuma 200, Sellier 232, Brunschvicg 347.
about.quote_link: Read the French text and edition concordance
about.source_soprano: inventory of 221 candidates and selection of 39 biases relevant to fact-checking.
about.source_dimara: taxonomy of 154 biases across seven task categories.
about.source_codex: historical visualisation of 188 entries, used for discovery rather than as scientific evidence.
about.method_note: Each card also links to a scientific publication specific to the phenomenon. Scores are provisional and will be reviewed using frequency, severity, range of domains and actionability.
about.footer: Bien penser — a critical catalogue of cognitive biases

leaderboard.intro: This ranking combines personal ratings from 1 to 100. It replaces neither the strength of scientific evidence nor the editorial importance score.
leaderboard.title: Bias ranking
leaderboard.note: A score is marked provisional when it is based on fewer than three ratings. Ties are broken by the number of voters.
